newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA says lost interest in Pemex refinery.
newsitem.headline: ICA says lost interest in Pemex refinery.

text.p: A spokesperson for Empresas ICA said on Tuesday that the Mexican construction firm is no longer interested in a $1.2 billion Caderyta refinery expansion.
"Officially we have not yet turned in the letter declining participation, but ICA no longer wants to enter," a spokesman who declined to be named told Reuters.

The due date for the project's bids was delayed two months to late August, with a decision expected in October. Analysts said an initial number of more than 10 vying firms has dwindled due to the project's demanding financing scheme.
They have said the northern refinery currently has just one strong contender, the announced consortia between Mexican constructor and Japanese Mitsubishi, Mitsui and Itochu.
The lack of interest from ICA and its partner Fluor Corp. follows Italian Snam Progetti also declining to bid.

Snam Progetti, controlled by the ENI group, dropped out of the bidding saying the financing was "too risky." It said the constructor must finance the three-year project out of its own pocket and be paid back over ten years.
But state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) director general Adrian Lajous has said that interest in the project is strong.
The Cadereyta expansion aims at processing fuel oil into gasolines and better quality fuel oil.

Constructors have said they are more interested in a different Pemex expansion, for the Cantarell crude oil field. ICA has said it is eyeing the $1 billion project to create a nitrogen plant, to be used for exploration in the region.
